angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 10,973,276 km at 112.74 pc = 1.3 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 79043: distance 112.74 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.062), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 112.74 +/- 6.99 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 8.2812 +/- 0.0922 mas (same row, RUWE 1.08), 89.8 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 15.773 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 79043: radius 15.773 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 132.468 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.08) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 10,973,276 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4934 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 79043: effective temperature 4934 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.105) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 79043: effective temperature 4934 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.105) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
